alignments.definition: Persistent divergence across retail formats in sales/network/unit-economics direction rather than uniform retail recovery or decline.
alignments.boundary: Does not imply that any format is a profitable operator opportunity, that format-level growth causes unit economics, or that individual stores share the aggregate result.
counterexamples: All major formats converge to similar growth and unit-economics direction.
Observed divergence disappears outside one short measurement window.
alignments.alignment_rationale: Official format growth plus independent industry observations show materially different trajectories across convenience, supermarket and other formats, but current reviewed support is still below the default observation-count gate.

alignments.definition: A repeated state in which smaller operators remain below expansion/comfort thresholds despite stronger aggregate demand signals elsewhere.
alignments.boundary: Does not assert that all small enterprises are distressed, that demand recovery bypasses every small firm, or that unused capability is currently callable.
counterexamples: Small-enterprise activity rises above expansion thresholds with improving revenue and cash runway.
Survey pressure is limited to one unrepresentative sector or temporary episode.
alignments.alignment_rationale: Official small-manufacturing PMI and longitudinal micro/small operator survey both show pressure, but two observations are insufficient to establish a promoted taxonomy concept.

alignments.definition: Institutional actions that make recurring home services more legible and auditable through standards, verification, routing, service records and cross-care integration.
alignments.boundary: Does not prove household willingness to prepay, platform adoption, lower failure rates, paid demand, or that one private orchestrator should own the workflow.
counterexamples: Recurring home services transact efficiently without verification, standardization or routing infrastructure.
Infrastructure is announced but produces no operational adoption or trust improvement.
alignments.alignment_rationale: National and Jiangsu policy actions converge on formalization, verification, routing and care integration, but current evidence is policy behavior rather than observed market outcomes.

alignments.definition: Recurring trust and exit friction in prepaid service relationships, including performance shrinkage, merchant disappearance, refund difficulty and information opacity.
alignments.boundary: Does not imply all prepaid services fail, does not estimate a national incident rate, and does not itself identify a better monetization model.
counterexamples: Prepaid-service complaint and disappearance rates fall materially with reliable refund/escrow mechanisms.
Observed issues are isolated to one locality or enforcement campaign.
alignments.alignment_rationale: Official risk guidance and local complaint statistics point to the same trust-friction family, but support remains too sparse for promotion review.

alignments.definition: A cross-level reallocation in which service and selected convenience/online categories can expand faster than headline consumption aggregates.
alignments.boundary: Does not infer consumer psychology, 'consumption upgrading', willingness to pay for arbitrary services, or causality from service-sector growth to household preference.
counterexamples: Service spending share and service-category growth converge with or fall below headline consumption over sustained periods.
Observed differences are entirely price effects without real volume or allocation change.
alignments.alignment_rationale: National household spending, Jiangsu consumption flows and Xuzhou service-sector growth all point toward service/value reallocation, while motive and category-level causality remain unknown.

alignments.definition: A multi-actor system behavior that combines demand-side support, medical/care capacity reconfiguration, heterogeneous designated providers and delegated administration to organize long-term-care delivery.
alignments.boundary: Supports only an observed organization/reconfiguration structure. It does not prove unmet demand, private orchestrator opportunity, provider spare capacity, payer identity for a new route, repeated settlement, transaction blockers, standardizable intervention or compounding.
counterexamples: The cited programs remain administratively separate and do not participate in a recurring care-delivery system.
Designated providers are nominal only and capacity reconfiguration is not implemented.
Administration awards do not translate into actual coordinated service delivery.
alignments.alignment_rationale: Four independent observations across Jiangsu/Xuzhou, multiple actor groups and multiple periods coherently describe organization of eldercare capacity; this is sufficient only for ontology promotion review under current diversity gates.
